new_entities.name: Food-sensitivity IgG testing
new_entities.description: Commercial measurement of food-specific IgG antibodies used to guide elimination diets for presumed food sensitivities.

new_entities.name: Symptom relief
new_entities.description: Improvement in patient-reported symptom burden or overall symptom severity.

edges.effect_quant: A 2026 systematic scoping review covering 13 intervention studies and 935 IBS patients found some symptom improvements in IgG-guided elimination-diet studies, but the evidence base remained methodologically weak and heterogeneous. In the best-known 150-patient randomized IBS trial, the true IgG-guided diet produced a 10% greater symptom-score reduction than sham, rising to 26% among fully compliant participants.
edges.population: mostly adults with irritable bowel syndrome or related functional symptom syndromes undergoing IgG-guided elimination diets
edges.mechanism: The proposed mechanism is that food-specific IgG identifies symptom-triggering foods, but IgG responses may also reflect routine exposure and tolerance rather than clinically meaningful hypersensitivity.
edges.summary: This edge should be treated as contested rather than clinically settled. Small or open-label studies often report symptom improvement, but the broader literature does not validate food-IgG panels as a dependable way to generate symptom-relieving elimination diets.
edges.caveats: Do not treat a positive food-IgG panel as equivalent to proven allergy or intolerance. Much of the apparent benefit may reflect nonspecific elimination effects, expectation effects, or dietary simplification rather than test-specific accuracy.

evidence.citation: Zuidmeer L et al 2026 Nutr Rev
